description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between model accuracy (ACC, in percent) and the co-occurrence number of biomedical entities, comparing six different model variants: Base (black solid line with circular markers), FT (blue solid line with triangular markers), IKE (red solid line with triangular markers), MEND (brown solid line with diamond markers), MEMIT (purple solid line with diamond markers), and ROME (green solid line with square markers). The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 1 to 10³, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 60% to 85%, with major tick marks at 65%, 70%, 75%, 80%, and 85%. All six lines show a positive trend, with accuracy increasing as co-occurrence number increases. At the lowest co-occurrence number (~1), Base starts at approximately 66%, FT at ~68%, IKE at ~69.5%, MEND at ~73%, MEMIT at ~71.5%, and ROME at ~76%. At the highest co-occurrence number (10³), Base reaches ~83%, FT ~86%, IKE ~88%, MEND ~89.5%, MEMIT ~88.5%, and ROME ~90%. ROME consistently maintains the highest accuracy across all co-occurrence levels, while Base consistently remains the lowest.
